questions.question: If a man deposits Rs. 12,100 in a bank at a simple interest of 15% per annum, then how much money will he receive from the bank after 3 years?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Type = Simple

Principle = Rs. 12,100

Rate = 15%

Time = 3 years

**Formula used:**

SI = (P x R x T) /100

A = SI + P

here, 

A = Amount

SI = Simple Interest

P = Principle

R = Rate

T = Time

**Solution:**

Let's put the values given, in the formula to find the value of SI;

SI = (12100 x 15 x 3) /100 = 5445

Now,

A = 12100 + 5445 = 17545

**Hence, he will get Rs. 17,545 at the end of 3rd year.**

questions.question: A borrows a sum of ₹90,000 for 4 years at 5% simple interest. He lends it to B at 7% for 4 years at simple interest. What is his gain (in ₹)
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Net gain rate = Lending rate − Borrowing rate = 7% − 5% = 2% per year.

Total gain percentage over 4 years = 2% × 4 = 8%.

Total Gain = 8% of ₹90,000 = (8 ÷ 100) × 90,000 = ₹7,200.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹7,200.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Principal (P) = ₹90,000

Rate of borrowing (R₁) = 5% per annum

Rate of lending (R₂) = 7% per annum

Time (T) = 4 years

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

Gain = Interest Received − Interest Paid

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/23fd7a27e8765482f39d9a80d01620f4f1ffc248fd824e31e248206ac61f4fed.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Interest paid by A to the lender = (90,000 × 5 × 4) ÷ 100

⇒ Interest paid by A = 900 × 20 = ₹18,000

⇒ Interest received by A from B = (90,000 × 7 × 4) ÷ 100

⇒ Interest received by A = 900 × 28 = ₹25,200

⇒ Total Gain = Interest Received − Interest Paid

⇒ Total Gain = 25,200 − 18,000 = ₹7,200

**∴ The correct answer is ₹7,200.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Simple Interest Formula

SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100, where P is the principal, R is the rate of interest per annum, and T is the time in years.

Difference in Simple Interest

When the principal and the time period are the same, the difference in Simple Interest is directly proportional to the difference in their rates: ΔSI = [P × T × (R₁ − R₂)] ÷ 100.

Simple vs Compound Interest

For the first year, both Simple Interest and Compound Interest (compounded annually) are exactly identical. From the second year onwards, Compound Interest grows faster as it calculates interest on the accumulated interest as well.

questions.question: A sum of ₹1,456, when invested for ten years, amounts to ₹2,366 on maturity. Find the rate of simple interest per annum that was to be paid on the sum invested.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Simple Interest for 10 years = ₹2,366 − ₹1,456 = ₹910.

Interest for 1 year = ₹910 ÷ 10 = ₹91.

Rate % = (Interest for 1 year ÷ Principal) × 100

Rate % = (91 ÷ 1456) × 100 = 6.25%.

**∴ The correct answer is 6.25%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Principal (P) = ₹1,456

Amount (A) = ₹2,366

Time (T) = 10 years

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (I) = Amount (A) − Principal (P)

Rate (R) = (I × 100) ÷ (P × T)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/24427a7c0e2205c03ff19dc6069f551a8e71b4ea5e60812d85464c96608d0700.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ SI = ₹2,366 − ₹1,456

⇒ SI = ₹910

⇒ R = (910 × 100) ÷ (1456 × 10)

⇒ R = 91000 ÷ 14560

⇒ R = 9100 ÷ 1456

⇒ R = 25 ÷ 4

⇒ R = 6.25%

**∴ The correct answer is 6.25%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Simple Interest (SI)

It is the interest calculated only on the initial principal amount. The principal remains constant throughout the tenure. Formula: SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100.

Amount (A)

It is the total sum of money payable at the end of the time period, which includes the original principal and the interest accumulated. Formula: A = P + SI.

Compound Interest (CI)

Interest calculated on both the initial principal and the accumulated interest from previous periods. Formula: A = P(1 + R ÷ 100)T.

questions.question: A certain sum of money is given at a certain rate of simple interest for 6 years. Had it been given at 7% higher rate, it would have fetched ₹1,512 more. Find the sum (in ₹).
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total additional interest percentage = Time × Extra Rate = 6 × 7% = 42%

This 42% additional interest on the principal corresponds to ₹1512.

Since Principal is always exactly 100%, we calculate:

Principal (100%) = (1512 ÷ 42) × 100

Principal = 36 × 100 = ₹3600

**∴ The correct answer is ₹3600.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time (T) = 6 years

Increase in Rate of Interest = 7%

Increase in Simple Interest = ₹1512

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

Difference in SI = (P × Change in Rate × T) ÷ 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/50d33c87fb761de75ae632ec99670dce420c9d71476105aedf523388997fc6e8.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the initial principal sum be P.

⇒ The additional interest earned is strictly due to the extra 7% rate applied over the 6 years duration.

⇒ Total extra interest percentage = 7% × 6 = 42%

⇒ According to the question, this 42% of P equals ₹1512.

⇒ (42 ÷ 100) × P = 1512

⇒ P = (1512 × 100) ÷ 42

⇒ P = 36 × 100

⇒ P = 3600

**∴ The correct answer is ₹3600.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Direct Proportionality in Simple Interest

Simple Interest is directly proportional to the Principal, Rate, and Time. If only the Rate increases by an amount, say r%, the extra interest is calculated directly as Extra SI = (P × r × T) ÷ 100.

Amount in Simple Interest

The final amount obtained after time T is the sum of the Principal and the accumulated Simple Interest. Formula: A = P + SI = P × [1 + (R × T) ÷ 100].

Simple Interest vs Compound Interest

In Simple Interest, the principal remains the same every year and interest does not compound. In Compound Interest, the interest earned in previous years is added back to the principal, yielding interest on interest.

questions.question: Money was lent on simple interest. After 12 years, its simple interest becomes (3)/(5) of the money. Find the rate of interest.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total Simple Interest percentage = (3 ÷ 5) × 100 = 60%

We know directly that Total SI% = Rate × Time

60% = Rate × 12

Rate = 60 ÷ 12 = 5%

**∴ The correct answer is 5% p.a.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

⇒ Let the Principal amount be P and the Rate of interest be R% p.a.

⇒ Given Time (T) = 12 years

⇒ Simple Interest (SI) after 12 years = (3 ÷ 5) × P

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c83b0ae8cac415066ebd2fb6682632b4c893a8f081ab948cacb5eadbf1765884.png] 

⇒ Formula: Simple Interest = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

⇒ (3 ÷ 5) × P = (P × R × 12) ÷ 100

⇒ 3 ÷ 5 = (12 × R) ÷ 100

⇒ R = (3 × 100) ÷ (5 × 12)

⇒ R = 300 ÷ 60

⇒ R = 5

**∴ The correct answer is 5% p.a.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Simple Interest vs Compound Interest

Simple Interest is strictly calculated only on the principal amount, whereas Compound Interest is calculated on the principal amount as well as the accumulated interest from previous periods.

Difference between CI and SI

For 2 years, Difference = P × (R ÷ 100)². For 3 years, Difference = P × (R ÷ 100)² × (3 + R ÷ 100).

Compound Interest Formula

Amount = P × (1 + R ÷ 100)ⁿ, where n is the number of years or compounding periods. The Compound Interest is obtained by subtracting the Principal from the Amount (CI = Amount − P).

questions.question: The simple interest on a certain sum of money at the rate of 8% p.a. for 9 years is ₹2,880. At what rate of interest can the same amount of interest can be received on the same sum for 12 years?

questions.question: In how much time will ₹5,000 at 4% per annum simple interest produce the same interest as ₹8,000 in 2(1)/(2) years at 8% per annum simple interest?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Since the simple interest in both cases is the same, we can equate P × R × T directly.

P₁ × R₁ × T₁ = P₂ × R₂ × T₂

5000 × 4 × T₁ = 8000 × 8 × 2.5

20000 × T₁ = 160000 ⇒ T₁ = 8

**∴ The correct answer is 8 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Principal for case 1 (P₁) = ₹5,000

Rate of interest for case 1 (R₁) = 4%

Principal for case 2 (P₂) = ₹8,000

Rate of interest for case 2 (R₂) = 8%

Time for case 2 (T₂) = 2.5 years

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/02acb456394164cf5f70d3303024986b6a27a7f36d1c472d7f4399cbc45fe799.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Interest for case 2 = (8000 × 8 × 2.5) ÷ 100

⇒ Interest for case 2 = 160000 ÷ 100 = ₹1600

⇒ Interest for case 1 = (5000 × 4 × T₁) ÷ 100 = 200 × T₁

Since the simple interest produced is the same for both cases:

⇒ 200 × T₁ = 1600

⇒ T₁ = 1600 ÷ 200

⇒ T₁ = 8 years

**∴ The correct answer is 8 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Total Amount in Simple Interest

The total amount (A) after T years is the sum of Principal and Simple Interest: A = P × [1 + (R × T) ÷ 100].

Equating Simple Interests

When two different sums yield the same simple interest, the relation P₁ × R₁ × T₁ = P₂ × R₂ × T₂ always holds true as the denominator 100 cancels out from both sides.

Effective Rate Percentage

In Simple Interest, the effective interest rate for T years is calculated simply by R × T %. For instance, 8% for 2.5 years generates an overall effective rate of 20% on the given principal.
